paragraphs: Security agents need executable vulnerability tasks for evaluation and training, but reproducing those tasks manually is expensive and can leave benchmarks outdated. CVE-Factory automates the conversion of sparse vulnerability metadata into runnable tasks. Its multi-agent process is evaluated against human expert reproductions rather than judged only by whether generated descriptions sound plausible.

The framework achieves 95% solution correctness and 96% environment fidelity in that comparison, alongside 66.2% verified success on recent realistic vulnerabilities. It supports LiveCVEBench, containing 190 tasks across 14 languages and 153 repositories, and the construction of more than 1,000 executable training environments.

Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on the generated environments raises reported LiveCVEBench performance from 5.3% to 35.8%, with improvements also appearing on Terminal Bench. The contribution links automated benchmark construction to measurable agent training gains. The success and fidelity figures describe the evaluated reproductions; they do not imply every automatically generated vulnerability environment is correct.
icml-2026-cve-factory-scaling-expert-lev.tldr: CVE-Factory turns vulnerability metadata into validated executable tasks, enabling a live benchmark and effective security-agent training data.

paragraphs: Matching markets become difficult to learn in when participants arrive and leave independently. Existing bandit models often assume everyone starts together and shares a global clock, simplifying coordination unrealistically. This paper studies learning preferences with only local timing and limited visibility into other participants’ outcomes.

For one-sided learning with uncoordinated arrivals, Way-SE coordinates exploration implicitly and obtains logarithmic-in-horizon regret with additional dependence on the number of arms and minimum utility gap. The authors then extend to two-sided learning with arbitrary arrivals and departures through Way-SE-2S. That algorithm operates without global signals or restrictive preference structures.

The two-sided method achieves a sublinear regret bound in the studied dynamic setting, giving a theoretical guarantee for fully decentralized, uncoordinated matching. The contribution is a way to learn toward stable matching despite missing synchronization. The exact rate depends strongly on market size and utility gaps, so sublinear regret alone does not imply uniformly rapid adaptation in every market.
icml-2026-decentralized-bandits-without-.tldr: Way-SE algorithms provide regret guarantees for dynamic matching markets whose participants learn without a global clock.

paragraphs: Vision-language driving systems increasingly use reasoning modules, but those modules are often adapted from general tasks without modeling driving-specific futures. DeepSight adds a world-modeling component focused on how the scene may evolve over a longer horizon. The aim is to improve decisions beyond immediate image interpretation.

The model predicts latent semantic features for consecutive future frames in bird’s-eye-view space, doing so in parallel. An additional adaptive text-reasoning mechanism supplies social knowledge and reasoning for difficult long-tail situations. These components combine anticipated scene structure with context that may be harder to capture through visual prediction alone.

The system achieves state-of-the-art results on the closed-loop Bench2Drive benchmark. The contribution is a driving-oriented combination of latent future modeling and selective text reasoning. Closed-loop benchmark performance provides evidence about the tested driving scenarios, while the abstract does not establish real-world road safety or reliable behavior in every rare event.
icml-2026-deepsight-long-horizon-world-m.tldr: DeepSight combines parallel prediction of future BEV features with adaptive text reasoning to improve closed-loop driving performance.

paragraphs: Generating a video with several personalized subjects requires preserving each identity across frames without mixing their attributes. Existing methods can also become expensive as more reference subjects are added. DiasR tackles identity consistency and computation together through alignment and sparse token routing.

Learnable identity queries align visual and textual information with subject masks. A sparse routing strategy then sends video tokens to relevant subjects and aggregates them into buckets, reducing redundant computation and identity entanglement. The authors also introduce MuSA-2M, a dataset with two million annotated samples and subject-level masks.

On OpenS2V-Eval, DiasR improves identity consistency, text fidelity, and video naturalness over the compared baselines. Inference time remains nearly constant as the number of reference subjects increases in the reported tests. The contribution combines training data and a subject-aware architecture; the scaling observation is empirical, not a guarantee for arbitrarily many subjects or every video length.
icml-2026-diasr-dual-modal-identity-anch.tldr: DiasR uses identity-aligned representations and sparse subject routing to improve multi-subject video quality and efficiency.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models can draft tokens in parallel, but weaker token dependencies can reduce quality relative to autoregressive models. Direct importance sampling between their distributions may require too many candidates. PoE-Bridge introduces an intermediate distribution to make that correction more efficient.

The bridge is a product of the diffusion proposal and autoregressive target. Parallel drafts first pass through rejection sampling that moves candidates toward the bridge; importance sampling then corrects them toward the target. Mixed-temperature sampling improves diversity, while elastic rejection windows reduce wasted verification work.

On mathematical reasoning and coding tasks, the framework improves accuracy with a reported fivefold speedup over standard diffusion-model decoding and recovers at least 95% of the target autoregressive model’s performance. The contribution combines complementary generators through a staged sampling procedure. Those performance ratios refer to the evaluated tasks and decoding comparison, rather than proving identical outputs or universal runtime gains.
icml-2026-diffusion-language-model-paral.tldr: A product-of-experts bridge improves correction between parallel diffusion drafts and an autoregressive target, boosting reported speed and quality.

paragraphs: Compute-in-memory hardware can reduce inference energy, but device noise and drift perturb model weights and degrade predictions. This paper trains networks to tolerate those hardware uncertainties. Diversity-aware Weight Perturbation uses differences in sample predictions under varied noise realizations to decide where training effort should concentrate.

The adaptive sample-weighting rule is inspired by affinity-based selection in immune systems. By emphasizing disagreement produced by diverse perturbations, the method encourages robustness to changes in deployed weights. The relevant uncertainty comes from hardware behavior, rather than only input noise or ordinary distribution shift.

Experiments report accuracy improvements above 15% over standard training under severe perturbations and around 90% accuracy through a simulated year of operation with small variation. A matched low-precision deployment reduces inference energy by 38% relative to a GPU baseline. The long-term stability result is simulated, and the energy comparison applies to the stated matched configurations.
icml-2026-diversity-aware-weight-perturb.tldr: Diversity-aware noise training improves robustness to compute-in-memory weight perturbations while supporting the reported energy-efficient deployment.

paragraphs: Activation verbalization asks one language model to describe another model’s internal representations in words. Those descriptions may seem insightful without revealing anything unavailable from the original input. This paper tests whether such methods actually convey privileged information about the target model’s internal computation.

The authors first show that popular evaluation benchmarks can be performed well without accessing target activations. They then run controlled experiments that separate knowledge in the target model from knowledge in the verbalizer. The resulting descriptions often reflect the verbalizer’s own learned information rather than the knowledge of the model being interpreted.

The findings call for targeted benchmarks and controls that can distinguish genuine internal access from plausible input-based explanation. The contribution is a methodological critique supported by experiments, not a claim that every activation-decoding approach is useless. It shows why fluent descriptions and good existing benchmark scores are insufficient evidence of faithful insight into model internals.
icml-2026-do-activation-verbalization-me.tldr: Activation verbalizations can reflect inputs and the verbalizer’s own knowledge, exposing weaknesses in current interpretability evaluations.

paragraphs: Conceptual aircraft design combines discrete choices about configuration with continuous choices about dimensions and other parameters. This paper uses simulation-based inference to learn a posterior over that mixed design space for electric vertical-takeoff-and-landing aircraft. The goal is to generate plausible designs efficiently while retaining the structure of the engineering problem.

A hierarchical probabilistic model uses two diffusion components. The first samples aircraft topologies using ideas from Riemannian diffusion language modeling and unified world models. The second uses masked diffusion to generate continuous parameters conditioned on the selected topology, respecting the fact that different configurations require different parameter sets.

The method rediscovers known design trends and governing physical laws while accelerating design generation. The contribution is a structured generative approach to conceptual engineering exploration. The abstract does not report flight testing, certification, or a guarantee that every sampled concept is manufacturable, so the results concern model-assisted design generation rather than finished aircraft.
icml-2026-do-diffusion-models-dream-of-e.tldr: A hierarchical diffusion model generates aircraft configurations and their continuous parameters through simulation-based inference.

paragraphs: Sensor streams vary over time and contain patterns at different scales, making fixed tokenization inefficient or poorly aligned with meaningful events. Dywave builds adaptive representations for heterogeneous Internet-of-Things signals. Its goal is to preserve temporal structure while compressing intervals that contribute little new information.

The framework uses hierarchical wavelet decomposition to identify meaningful temporal boundaries. It then compresses redundant segments adaptively while maintaining coherence across the sequence. This makes token lengths respond to the signal’s own structure instead of imposing the same granularity on every interval.

Across five real-world datasets covering activity recognition, stress assessment, and nearby-object detection, Dywave improves accuracy by up to 12% and reduces input-token lengths by up to 75%. It also shows better robustness to domain shifts and changing sequence lengths. These are maximum reported gains across evaluated settings, rather than a guaranteed simultaneous improvement for every sensor or downstream model.
icml-2026-dywave-event-aligned-dynamic-t.tldr: Dywave aligns sensor tokens with temporal events, improving reported accuracy while substantially shortening input sequences.

paragraphs: Estimating full-hand grasp pressure from a wearable camera could reduce reliance on intrusive tactile hardware. Existing visual methods often focus on fingertips or planar contacts, missing complex interactions with everyday objects. EgoTactile introduces data and models for that richer estimation problem.

The benchmark pairs egocentric video with full-hand pressure supervision and includes a bare-hand transfer subset. The authors establish EgoPressureFormer as a discriminative baseline, then propose EgoPressureDiff to represent uncertainty from partial views. The diffusion model adapts a pretrained video backbone and adds physically informed feature rectification to guide plausible contact patterns.

Experiments show stronger benchmark performance and transfer to in-the-wild scenarios. The contribution combines a dataset with an uncertainty-aware pressure predictor. Because hidden contacts are inferred from incomplete visual information, plausible generated patterns should be distinguished from direct tactile measurement; the abstract does not claim that every individual pressure estimate is physically exact.
icml-2026-egotactile-learning-grasp-pres.tldr: EgoTactile pairs egocentric video with full-hand pressure labels and uses conditional diffusion to infer plausible grasp patterns.

paragraphs: Language models used in conversation must interpret emotional language, but the structure and biases of that interpretation are not fully understood. This paper examines whether model outputs organize emotions hierarchically, as proposed by psychological emotion-wheel frameworks. It studies probabilistic dependencies among emotional states rather than attributing subjective feelings to the models.

The analysis finds emotion trees that align with human psychological models, with larger language models developing more complex hierarchies. The authors also test recognition across socioeconomic personas and identify systematic errors, including compounded misclassification for intersectional, underrepresented groups. Human studies reveal parallels in patterns of social perception.

The contribution connects an emergent organization in model outputs with concrete fairness concerns in emotion recognition. It also suggests cognitively grounded theories as tools for evaluation. The results concern how models represent and classify emotional information; they do not establish that models experience emotions or that their classifications reliably reveal a person’s actual internal state.
icml-2026-emergence-of-hierarchical-emot.tldr: LLM outputs exhibit hierarchical emotion structure alongside socioeconomic and intersectional recognition biases.

paragraphs: Conformal classification returns a set of plausible labels with a coverage guarantee, but users may also care whether those labels belong to many unrelated semantic groups. A set containing several closely related classes can be easier to act on than an equally sized scattered set. This paper incorporates class similarity into the conformal score.

Given a class partition, the method adds a penalty for out-of-group errors. Theoretical analysis shows improvements in group-related measures and, for common partitions, smaller average prediction sets. The authors then use model embeddings to capture similarity without requiring a manually specified semantic grouping.

An extensive evaluation spans conformal methods, models, and datasets and finds consistent improvements. The contribution is a score modification informed by relationships among labels, with theory explaining why it can help both group coherence and set size. Coverage guarantees still belong to the conformal framework’s conditions; the abstract does not imply perfect label identification for each individual example.
icml-2026-enhancing-conformal-prediction.tldr: Class-similarity-aware conformal scores produce more coherent and often smaller prediction sets, including without manual class groupings.

paragraphs: Group Relative Policy Optimization normalizes rewards to guide language-model reasoning, but near-uniform reward groups can make standard-deviation scaling unstable. Multimodal tasks add another complication because failures may arise from either perception or reasoning. This paper uses estimated difficulty to organize normalization more reliably.

Difficulty combines visual entropy as a measure of perceptual complexity with model confidence as a measure of reasoning uncertainty. The proposed Durian method regroups examples by these difficulty levels and shares the standard deviation within each group. This aims to preserve useful relative distinctions while reducing sensitivity to extreme reward patterns.

Experiments show significant gains across several multimodal reasoning benchmarks. The contribution is a targeted modification to reward normalization rather than a new visual architecture or a different correctness verifier. The abstract does not specify numerical improvements or prove that its difficulty estimates perfectly separate perceptual from reasoning errors, but it provides evidence that the grouping is useful for training.
icml-2026-enhancing-multi-modal-llms-rea.tldr: Durian groups multimodal training examples by perceptual and reasoning difficulty to stabilize GRPO normalization and improve reasoning results.

paragraphs: Evolution strategies optimize parameters through population-based evaluations rather than backpropagating through the model. They are often assumed to scale poorly to very large language models. This paper challenges that assumption by applying evolution strategies to full-parameter fine-tuning at the billion-parameter scale without dimensionality reduction.

The study compares this approach with established reinforcement-learning implementations across several aspects of post-training. Reported advantages include tolerance of long-horizon and delayed rewards, robustness across base models, improved stability, and reduced susceptibility to reward hacking. These tests examine how the optimization paradigm behaves, not simply whether it can update a large parameter vector.

The findings establish a viable alternative direction for large-model fine-tuning in the evaluated settings. The abstract does not supply training-cost comparisons or claim that evolution strategies dominate every reinforcement-learning method. Its contribution is a large-scale demonstration and comparative evidence that a backpropagation-free approach deserves consideration for tasks where its different optimization behavior is useful.
icml-2026-evolution-strategies-at-scale-.tldr: Full-parameter evolution strategies successfully fine-tune billion-parameter language models and show advantages over the evaluated RL implementations.

paragraphs: A dynamic graph can contain hierarchical, grid-like, and cyclic neighborhoods that change over time. Embedding every node in one fixed-curvature space may therefore mismatch local structure. DyGMoCE lets each node’s representation use an adaptive geometry as its neighborhood evolves.

The model is a graph Transformer with curvature-aware experts in both attention and feedforward modules. Each expert operates on a Riemannian manifold with a distinct curvature. A ranking-constrained router coordinates selection across geometrically related experts, and a fast Riemannian attention module reduces computational overhead.

Extensive experiments outperform compared dynamic-graph methods. The attention module reports an average 27.5% speedup and 52.6% memory reduction and is designed to extend to sequence-input Transformers. The contribution combines flexible representation geometry with efficiency improvements; the abstract does not specify that every node uses every geometry or that the reported average speedup holds for all graph sizes.
icml-2026-fast-mixture-of-curvature-awar.tldr: DyGMoCE routes dynamic-graph representations among curvature-specific experts while using faster, more memory-efficient Riemannian attention.

paragraphs: Aggregation-free federated learning shares synthetic data instead of directly aggregating local model updates. Its effectiveness depends on how faithfully those synthetic examples represent heterogeneous client data. FedUSD argues that existing approaches fail to separate principal structure from residual variation, leaving the shared synthetic data biased.

The method matches two feature-space properties of real and synthetic data: a High-energy Orthogonal Base for the principal component and variance for the residual component. The authors motivate this separation empirically and formulate synthetic-data optimization around both quantities. Their theory establishes unbiasedness and convergence under the analyzed construction.

Experiments show improved global-model performance at equivalent communication cost, including a difficult heterogeneous SVHN setting. The contribution is a more structured matching objective for synthetic-data federation. The abstract’s example improvement wording is ambiguous, so the reliable takeaway is the comparative gain rather than a reconstructed numerical interpretation of that example.
icml-2026-fedusd-unbiased-synthetic-data.tldr: FedUSD matches principal feature structure and residual variance to improve synthetic-data sharing in aggregation-free federated learning.

paragraphs: Pruning can make a language model repeatedly loop through the same text even when perplexity and benchmark accuracy change little. This paper studies that failure at the token level. It treats decoding as a dynamical process that can enter and remain in a small collection of recurrent contexts.

The analysis separates the risk of entering a loop from the difficulty of escaping it. Persistence depends on probability mass assigned to plausible alternatives in the sampling set. FOCUS reweights distillation toward confident teacher regions, while RePAIR trains on positive and negative continuations near repetition onset to discourage premature commitment to loops.

Across open-ended continuation and instruction-following generation, both methods reduce repetition and improve output quality. The contribution is a diagnosis and post-pruning training response to a failure that coarse metrics can hide. The abstract does not claim that these objectives eliminate all repetition or that every repeated phrase is an undesirable degeneration.
icml-2026-focus-repair-mitigating-text-d.tldr: FOCUS and RePAIR target loop entry and persistence to reduce repetition in pruned language models beyond what perplexity reveals.

paragraphs: Off-policy reinforcement learning may assign unrealistic values to actions poorly represented in its replay buffer. Frictional Q-Learning studies that extrapolation through a geometric analogy. Supported actions form a local manifold, and moving along it differs from moving away from it into weakly supported regions.

The analysis separates tangential directions from normal directions, with the latter capturing dominant first-order extrapolation error. This leads to a stability condition analogous to a friction threshold. A contrastive variational autoencoder represents supported directions, while an orthogonal-complement construction identifies normal components under local-isometry assumptions.

Experiments on standard continuous-control benchmarks show robust, stable performance against competitive baselines. The contribution is a geometry-based way to discourage harmful departures from observed action support. The manifold and local-isometry assumptions define the theoretical interpretation, so the analogy should not be read as a guarantee that all extrapolation errors vanish in arbitrary replay distributions.
icml-2026-frictional-q-learning-b1616fb3.tldr: Frictional Q-Learning uses action-support geometry to reduce unstable value extrapolation toward poorly observed actions.

paragraphs: Poorly conditioned kernel matrices can slow first-order neural-network training. This paper analyzes whether Gauss–Newton updates avoid that bottleneck in both underparameterized and overparameterized settings. It provides finite-time convergence guarantees rather than relying only on local intuition about second-order optimization.

For underparameterized networks, parameter-space dynamics induce a Riemannian gradient flow on a lower-dimensional manifold of functions. With appropriate output scaling, geometric smoothness and Polyak–Łojasiewicz conditions yield geometric convergence to the best predictor in the model class. The rate does not depend on Gram-matrix conditioning.

For overparameterized networks, adaptive curvature-aware damping gives geometric convergence to a global optimum for both flow and discrete updates, independently of the minimum neural-tangent-kernel eigenvalue. The contribution explains when Gauss–Newton can be provably faster in ill-conditioned regimes. These iteration guarantees do not by themselves quantify the computational cost of forming or solving each Gauss–Newton update.
icml-2026-geometric-convergence-of-gauss.tldr: Geometric analysis and adaptive damping give Gauss–Newton convergence rates that avoid conditioning bottlenecks in specified neural-network regimes.

paragraphs: Class-incremental learning must acquire new categories without damaging previously learned ones. Orthogonal gradient constraints help preserve old knowledge but can leave less room for learning as tasks accumulate. GR-LoRA aims to recover some of that lost adaptability by reusing gradient components that orthogonal projection would discard.

The method directs those nonorthogonal components into lightweight task-specific modules and uses entropy to select a suitable module. Local and global mismatch suppression, supported by synthesized out-of-distribution representations across tasks, helps preserve stability. This separates where potentially conflicting updates are stored while still letting them contribute to new-task learning.

Theoretical analysis supports improved plasticity with retained stability, and multiple class-incremental benchmarks validate the approach. The contribution is a parameter-efficient mechanism for managing the stability–plasticity tension. The abstract does not claim that all forgetting disappears indefinitely or specify how module storage grows across arbitrarily long task sequences.
icml-2026-gr-lora-gradient-recycling-low.tldr: GR-LoRA recycles otherwise discarded gradient components into lightweight modules to balance new-class learning with retention.

paragraphs: A vision-language model may encode spatial information internally yet produce an incorrect verbal answer. This paper identifies that representation-to-output mismatch through linear probes. GRASP then attempts to improve spatial answers during inference without updating model parameters.

Manifold Differential Search finds geometric counterfactuals that guide two forms of correction. Implicit Trajectory Correction strengthens geometric features in intermediate decoder layers, while Explicit Distribution Alignment reduces the dominance of language priors at the output. The framework therefore addresses both the propagation of spatial information and its expression in final text.

Across LLaVA and Qwen-based architectures, positional encodings, and image/video benchmarks, GRASP reduces spatial hallucinations. Reported accuracy gains reach 26.1% on image tasks and 9.7% on video reasoning. These results support inference-time geometric adjustment in the tested settings; successful probing alone would not have established that a model’s unmodified answers reliably use the encoded information.
icml-2026-grasp-awakening-latent-spatial.tldr: GRASP corrects internal and output representations at inference time to improve spatial reasoning without parameter updates.

paragraphs: Token-level watermarks for synthetic audio must survive the imperfect mapping between continuous sound and discrete tokens. Existing solutions can require retraining the tokenizer, reducing the appeal of inference-time watermarking. This paper instead exploits redundancy within the learned token vocabulary.

The authors analyze how token errors affect watermark detection and use community detection to form a reduced vocabulary. Grouping related tokens mitigates inconsistencies introduced during audio reconstruction and retokenization. The method is gradient-free, avoiding the tokenizer fine-tuning required by some earlier approaches.

Experiments report improvements in detectability by several orders of magnitude and robustness to audio modifications. The contribution is a representation-aware watermarking strategy that turns vocabulary redundancy into a useful resource. The abstract does not specify every tested transformation or a guarantee against arbitrary editing, so robustness should be understood relative to the evaluated audio modifications and detection setup.
icml-2026-hidden-in-plain-tokens-simply-.tldr: Grouping redundant audio tokens enables gradient-free watermarks with stronger reported detection and resistance to audio modifications.

paragraphs: Mamba can infer a new task from examples in a prompt, but its nonlinear gating makes that behavior difficult to analyze. This paper studies a one-layer model on unseen binary-classification tasks, including prompts contaminated by additive outliers. It seeks to explain both learning dynamics and robustness.

The analyzed model contains a linear-attention component followed by nonlinear gating. Attention selects informative context examples, while the gate suppresses outlier influence. The authors compare the resulting theory with a linear Transformer under the same setting, allowing differences in robustness and optimization speed to be attributed more clearly to the architecture.

Mamba can require more iterations to converge, but it retains accurate predictions beyond the outlier proportion tolerated by the compared linear Transformer. Experiments support the theory. The contribution is a mechanism and guarantee for a specified simplified model, rather than a universal statement that every Mamba architecture is more robust than every Transformer on arbitrary corrupted prompts.
icml-2026-how-can-mamba-learn-in-context.tldr: A one-layer theory shows how Mamba’s gating can suppress prompt outliers, trading slower convergence for stronger studied ICL robustness.

paragraphs: Estimating AI training emissions is difficult when developers disclose inconsistent amounts of energy, compute, and hardware information. This paper uses publicly available Hugging Face model metadata to build an accounting framework that works without reproducing training. It aims to quantify a broad collection of models despite incomplete records.

A tiered estimation approach adapts to the available emissions, energy, compute, and model information. Empirical regressions assess reliability where disclosures are incomplete. The authors also define AI training carbon intensity as emissions per unit of computation, providing a way to compare the sustainability efficiency of training processes.

The study estimates roughly 60,000 metric tons of training emissions for the analyzed models with more than 5,000 downloads. This is an estimate for a selected open-source population, not a measurement of all AI emissions or inference use. The contribution is scalable accounting under imperfect disclosure and a framework that could inform more consistent future reporting.
icml-2026-hugging-carbon-quantifying-the.tldr: Hugging Carbon estimates open-model training emissions from incomplete metadata and introduces emissions-per-compute accounting.

paragraphs: Long reasoning traces can improve answers while increasing inference cost. Sequence-level rewards give limited control over which individual steps are worth that cost. IAPO introduces token-level training signals intended to preserve useful reasoning while reducing low-value elaboration.

The framework assigns token-wise advantages using conditional mutual information between each token and the final answer. This information-theoretic criterion aims to distinguish steps that contribute to the answer from exploration with little utility. The authors analyze conditions under which the method reduces verbosity monotonically without harming correctness.

Across reasoning datasets, IAPO improves accuracy while shortening reasoning by up to 36%, outperforming the compared token-efficient reinforcement-learning methods. The contribution is a more granular way to allocate reasoning effort during post-training. The theoretical correctness statement belongs to the analyzed setting, while the empirical reduction is a maximum reported gain rather than a guaranteed compression ratio for every problem.
icml-2026-iapo-information-aware-policy-.tldr: IAPO shapes token-level advantages by answer-relevant information, improving reported reasoning accuracy while reducing trace length.
